stem: One wall sensor shows normal RH while affected plants cluster inside a dense canopy. Which next step has the highest diagnostic value?
choices: Average the wall reading with the previous shift's room average to decide whether the controller is broadly representative.
Map temperature and RH at representative canopy positions, including affected and unaffected areas, and compare those measurements with the wall sensor.
Adjust the dehumidification target slightly and watch whether the affected cluster improves before spending time on additional measurements.
Inspect root-zone EC and irrigation timing first because a normal wall RH makes a canopy-scale humidity difference less likely.
rationale: A single wall sensor can describe conditions at its location without representing the microclimate inside a dense canopy. Mapping temperature and RH across representative canopy positions, especially affected versus unaffected areas, tests whether the controller reading is spatially representative and whether a local environmental pattern tracks the symptoms. Averaging unrelated readings does not resolve spatial bias, changing a setpoint before verifying the pattern confounds the diagnosis, and moving directly to root-zone causes prematurely discounts a plausible canopy microclimate.
